[
  {
    "chunk_id": "U0011",
    "include": true,
    "question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
    "relevance": "Reports measured sovereign-yield, portfolio-flow, exchange-rate, reserve, and risk-spread outcomes; attributes peso stability to fiscal fundamentals, monetary commitment, remittances, and domestic pension-fund purchases; and records the government's USD 7 billion foreign-exchange purchase for public-sector debt amortization.",
    "adjacent_context": "The preceding page is needed to identify the omitted opening referent for the 20-year bond-yield increase; Annex V and the cited reserve methodology would qualify the flow and reserve findings.",
    "exclusion_reason": null
  },
  {
    "chunk_id": "U0012",
    "include": true,
    "question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.4", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
    "relevance": "Provides measured credit-recovery and banking-capital outcomes, including capital adequacy above 19 percent versus 16 percent before the pandemic; identifies public mortgage lending; and records fuel-price smoothing, above-budget subsidies, a six-month food-price agreement, temporary food-tariff reductions, distribution-cost measures, and production support focused on small farmers.",
    "adjacent_context": "The following page completes the PEMEX finding and is needed to assess how its improved earnings were allocated; Annex VI supplies the detailed design and fiscal incidence of the anti-inflation measures.",
    "exclusion_reason": null
  },
  {
    "chunk_id": "U0013",
    "include": true,
    "question_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
    "relevance": "Records PEMEX capital-expenditure and debt-amortization use of improved cash generation, persistent debt and elevated borrowing spreads, and concrete 2023 budget choices: a deficit increase from 3.8 to 4.1 percent of GDP, nominal expenditure growth of 8.5 percent, higher interest, pension, infrastructure, fertilizer, milk-procurement, and rural-supply spending, plus tax-enforcement efforts without a tax-code change. It also gives conditional growth, employment, current-account, and fiscal-stance projections.",
    "adjacent_context": "The preceding page supplies the source and magnitude of PEMEX's earnings increase; later fiscal-policy sections are needed to judge implementation quality, targeting, and debt sustainability rather than the proposal alone.",
    "exclusion_reason": null
  },
  {
    "chunk_id": "U0014",
    "include": true,
    "question_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.4", "5B.6", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
    "relevance": "Provides conditional inflation and interest-rate projections, a medium-term finding that growth would remain near 2 percent and per-capita potential growth only slightly above 1 percent absent significant structural reforms, and quantified downside scenarios involving output loss, capital outflows, liquidity stress, exchange-rate pressure, imported inflation, remittances, and Mexico's greater-than-one short-run GDP elasticity to U.S. GDP.",
    "adjacent_context": "The next page completes the risk inventory and identifies policy uncertainty, climate exposure, and potential nearshoring gains; Box 2 supplies the model specification behind the quantified global-inflation scenario.",
    "exclusion_reason": null
  },
  {
    "chunk_id": "U0015",
    "include": true,
    "question_ids": ["5B.4", "5B.7", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
    "relevance": "Identifies contrary medium-term findings that pandemic scarring, policy uncertainty, climate shocks, and stranded energy assets could reduce potential output, alongside possible nearshoring and trade-diversion gains. It also records differing official 2023 growth forecasts, the authorities' inflation mechanism and policy attribution, and their assessment of U.S. slowdown and capital-flow risks.",
    "adjacent_context": "The preceding page supplies the baseline growth and inflation projections; the cited annexes are required to evaluate nearshoring, trade-diversion, and U.S.-spillover methods and magnitudes.",
    "exclusion_reason": null
  },
  {
    "chunk_id": "U0016",
    "include": true,
    "question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
    "relevance": "States the IMF G20MOD multi-country DSGE method, layered shock design, assumptions, and limitations, and quantifies modeled effects: 10 percent oil and 50 percent food-price shocks raise Mexican inflation nearly 1 percentage point; expectation dislocation and rate increases lower output by more than 1 percent; an added 1 percent domestic-demand shock takes output more than 2 percent below baseline. It explicitly notes that a capital-flow shock is not modeled.",
    "adjacent_context": "The surrounding outlook establishes the baseline and policy setting against which these deviations are calculated; the accompanying FSSA contains the detailed liquidity-risk assessment.",
    "exclusion_reason": null
  },
  {
    "chunk_id": "U0017",
    "include": true,
    "question_ids": ["5B.2", "5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
    "relevance": "Documents Banxico's successive and increasingly large rate increases since June 2021, the resulting roughly 4 percent ex-ante real policy rate by September 2022, and the IMF's favorable calibration finding. It identifies an expected policy rate of at least 10 percent as necessary to return inflation near target and lists concrete sources of uncertainty affecting timing and durability.",
    "adjacent_context": "The following chunk completes the inflation-risk list and discusses rate-duration and communication responses; the referenced Banxico modeling supplies the neutral-rate benchmark.",
    "exclusion_reason": null
  },
  {
    "chunk_id": "U0018",
    "include": true,
    "question_ids": ["5B.2", "5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
    "relevance": "Gives empirical and methodological qualifications for further restrictive policy, including Phillips-curve estimates, asymmetric inflation risks, minimum-wage pass-through, and a projected ex-ante real rate above 5 percent in 2023. It documents Banxico's publication of updated inflation forecasts with every decision since August 2021 and forward guidance, assesses those measures as improving public understanding, and proposes additional disclosure of the forecast-consistent rate path and adjustment triggers.",
    "adjacent_context": "The prior chunk establishes the tightening already executed; the next page completes the proposal for reviewing the inflation-targeting and communications framework.",
    "exclusion_reason": null
  },
  {
    "chunk_id": "U0019",
    "include": true,
    "question_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
    "relevance": "Quantifies and evaluates anti-inflation measures: roughly 2 percent of GDP in largely untargeted subsidies; fuel-price stabilization lowering inflation by an estimated 2 percentage points at a cost near 1.5 percent of GDP while disproportionately benefiting richer households and weakening demand adjustment; and food measures with smaller cost but minimal direct inflation effect. It also records universal-pension and minimum-wage increases, an attributed 5 percent rise in real per-capita labor income, the limited net deficit effect, and the contrary risk that further wage increases could raise inflation and reduce formal employment among lower-income workers.",
    "adjacent_context": "Annex VI is needed for full program design and estimation details; the following chunk provides the authorities' competing interpretation and the income-incidence figures underlying the targeting critique.",
    "exclusion_reason": null
  },
  {
    "chunk_id": "U0020",
    "include": true,
    "question_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.6", "5B.7", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
    "relevance": "Records the authorities' attribution of smooth financial-market adjustment to stronger monetary communication and their claims about fuel stabilization, household support, underserved agricultural communities, and expected yield effects. It also identifies the limited countercyclical room under balanced-budget and debt-issuance constraints and proposes replacing broad fuel support with market-based pricing and targeted safety-net support. The cited incidence data show the top income quintile accounted for about 45 percent of fuel-excise payments versus 6 percent for the bottom quintile, supporting the finding of leakage to richer households.",
    "adjacent_context": "The preceding chunk supplies independent cost and outcome estimates for the same measures; the next page is needed to complete the proposed instruments for targeted support and fiscal-framework reform.",
    "exclusion_reason": null
  }
]
